patch_description: The current program's weakest metrics are smoothness (0.23), slope changes (66.8) and false reversals (48.0), while lag error (0.28) and correlation (0.96) are strong — meaning we have lag budget to spend on smoothness. Since the bidirectional one-pole passes are inherently zero-lag (forward+backward passes cancel phase), adding a third, milder pass increases smoothing depth nearly for free in lag. Additionally, making the smoothing strength noise-adaptive (stronger smoothing when the local residual variance is high relative to the estimated measurement noise, weaker when the signal is moving coherently) prevents over-smoothing genuine dynamics — protecting tracking accuracy and false-reversal behavior. Finally, a noise-scaled slope deadzone (suppressing output increments whose magnitude falls below a fraction of the estimated noise-induced step) directly attacks spurious slope changes: tiny jitter steps are flattened while real trend steps pass through. This preserves the validated structure and interface, only modifying the post-processing pipeline in enhanced_filter_with_trend_preservation plus a small helper.
